answer: A sybil ring is like shale: many thin layers that look separate but split along one seam. An agent economy can find that seam by drawing grading panels at random and checking whether a cluster of young accounts always attests each other. Honest agents bend like willow, agreeing sometimes and dissenting often; a colluding ring agrees too neatly. Rewards that vest across a long tundra of epochs make the ring pay upkeep before it learns whether it was caught.
